Catalog compilation does not install or execute upstream content.

currentClauses.text: Decision: Use one Control Plane core and one set of domain/execution contracts across three deployment profiles, with implementation sequence separated from Agent HQ product rollout.

Control Plane M9 first establishes the production-shaped managed-cloud reference on Railway using Restate, a separate Neon PostgreSQL database, Cloudflare R2 for explicitly cloud-stored artifacts/bundles, Railway service/shared variables for deployment/service bootstrap configuration, and replaceable coordination services where measured need justifies them.

M10 then ports that accepted core and workflow behavior to the developer-MVP user-controlled profiles.

Local is the default developer execution mode: Agent HQ packages and supervises the local Control Plane with embedded SQLite durable execution and persistence, local filesystem/object storage (Local Restate remains optional compatibility only), Cortana when enabled, managed Pi, and required RuntimeDrivers.
Ordinary desktop users do not install Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis/Valkey, or Temporal.
Co-located runtime execution uses a direct local IPC/in-process boundary rather than Runtime Gateway.

Self-hosted/VPS is also a first-class developer-MVP mode: the same Control Plane core runs on user-controlled infrastructure through supported Docker/Docker Compose profiles, with Restate and durable volumes, SQLite in simple mode, PostgreSQL recommended for server-grade mode, user-controlled object storage, and authenticated Runtime Gateway transport only when the selected runtime node is non-co-located.

The user-visible Agent HQ Cloud execution location remains a later consumer product feature even though M9 managed-cloud completion is accepted as the baseline; the full M11 cross-profile production-readiness audit and independent release decision remain open.

Agent HQ Cloud remains present during the developer MVP for authentication/accounts, workspace membership and cloud-safe product metadata, billing, node/host registration/revocation, product events/synchronization, and the durable web/mobile command/status relay.
Sensitive execution content stays on the selected user-controlled execution location by default.
If a Local or Self-hosted location is unavailable, Agent HQ reports/queues according to policy and never silently moves work into Agent HQ Cloud.

currentClauses.text: Rationale: The existing cloud/server implementation is the most mature production-shaped composition, so completing it on Railway first gives Local and Self-hosted work a concrete operational and semantic reference to port.

Developer users still benefit from Local execution through low latency, repository and credential access, reduced data collection, and a trust model that does not require source code, prompts, memory, or execution context to traverse Agent HQ infrastructure.
Self-hosting provides the same always-on benefits on user-controlled VPS/home-server infrastructure.
M10 can therefore focus on replacing deployment adapters and composition while continuously comparing against a known-good M9 cloud baseline.
The later Agent HQ consumer phase exposes managed always-on execution as a product feature without requiring a new Control Plane implementation.
A shared core minimizes duplicated implementation and semantic drift across execution locations.

Consequences: M9 owns every change required to make the first-party managed-cloud profile correct and operable, including Railway build/service configuration, managed-cloud Restate migration, Neon/R2 wiring, service authentication, bootstrap configuration, dynamic credential-vault provider selection/verification, networking, health/readiness, migrations, recovery, cloud security, and evidence of cost and performance under production conditions.

Deployment/service bootstrap secrets and dynamic user/provider credentials are separate classes: Railway variables may provide the former, while the latter stay behind the provider-neutral credential-vault secret-provider contract.
M9 also freezes deployment-independent public contracts, deterministic Profile/Skill/ContextProvider behavior, and global operational defaults before portability begins.

M10 starts only from that accepted cloud reference and owns Local/Self-hosted adapter/composition work: Self-hosted Restate packaging and optional Local Restate compatibility, shared infrastructure ports, SQLite, all-in-one composition, direct RuntimeTransport, user-controlled SecretsProvider adapters, Compose profiles, host-side HPKE remote control, cross-profile conformance, migration tooling, and user-controlled deployment hardening.
Persistence, object storage, secrets, coordination, process supervision, service discovery, observability, and runtime transport remain deployment adapters rather than domain dependencies.

Local and Self-hosted `simple` use Node 24 `node:sqlite` through Drizzle behind PersistenceProvider; Self-hosted `server` and managed cloud use PostgreSQL, with Neon selected for the first-party cloud profile.
Local/Self-hosted artifacts use user-controlled storage by default; Cloudflare R2 is used only for explicit first-party cloud storage/promotion.
Restate is canonical for Hosted/cloud and Self-hosted profiles; default Local uses the embedded SQLite durable queue, with optional Local Restate compatibility.
Runtime Gateway is a remote-node transport and is not required for co-located local execution.
Web/mobile remote control uses Agent HQ's durable relay; content-bearing commands/results use ADR-036 HPKE so Agent HQ Cloud can route ciphertext without plaintext prompt/context access.

Product configuration and core execution behavior remain portable across profiles; explicit migration/synchronization of histories or content is separate and never implied by changing execution location.
M11 release conformance re-runs managed cloud, Local, and Self-hosted together before M12 cross-product composition.
